items.title: How to Build $6,600 a Month in Dividend Income From Three Income Buckets
items.summary: Reaching $6,600 a month in dividend income sounds like a single-number problem, but the capital you actually need swings by more than a million dollars depending on which yield tier you choose and what you give up to get there.

items.title: How to Build $11,800 a Month in Dividend Income Without Selling a Single Share
items.summary: Collecting over $141,000 a year in dividends without selling a single share sounds like a fantasy until you realize the yield you chase determines whether your income grows, stagnates, or quietly cannibalizes itself.

items.title: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Wins EU Approval For TECVAYLI Combo In Multiple Myeloma
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) received European Commission approval for TECVAYLI®▼ (teclistamab) plus daratumumab for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. The decision allows use of the combination as early as second line for patients whose disease has returned or is not responding to prior treatment. The approval is based on Phase 3 data that showed material improvements in patient outcomes versus existing standards of care. This adds another immunotherapy option to Johnson...

items.title: The Portfolio Blueprint for Building $19,000 a Month in Dividend Income
items.summary: Generating $19,000 a month from dividends alone sounds like a single problem with one answer, but the yield you chase changes the required nest egg by millions and introduces a completely different set of risks, tax consequences, and long-term tradeoffs.

items.title: How a 53-Year-Old Can Turn $465,000 Into a Monthly Paycheck Machine by 63
items.summary: Starting yield and dividend growth pull $465,000 in two very different directions over a decade, and choosing the wrong one at 53 could cost you far more than the yield gap suggests.

items.title: Lilly's Multiple Assumes Less Growth Than You Think
items.summary: Consensus asks Eli Lilly for far less growth than it is delivering, and for margins to keep climbing from a level it only just reached.

items.title: Intuitive Surgical Stock Has Fallen While Its Operating Margin Keeps Widening
items.summary: With US procedure growth slowing and the shares well below their high, the operating margin has widened in each of the last three years.

items.title: Most Of What Moves AbbVie Stock Has Nothing To Do With The Market
items.summary: What AbbVie sells, and who pays for it, is the useful way to read its low correlation to the index.
